dedupe_keys.name: cape open interoperability standard for process simulation

description: CAPE-OPEN is a series of specifications of software interfaces that allow plug and play interoperability between a process modelling environment, such as a flowsheet simulator, and third-party process modelling components such as thermodynamic property packages, unit operations, chemical reactions or numerical solvers. It began as a European Union funded project in 1997 with process companies (Bayer, BASF, BP, DuPont, IFP, Elf Aquitaine, ICI), software vendors and universities, followed by the Global CAPE-OPEN project, which founded the non-profit CAPE-OPEN Laboratories Network (CO-LaN) to maintain the standard. Specifications cover thermodynamics and physical properties (versions 1.0 and 1.1), unit operations, petroleum fractions, chemical reactions, physical property databases, numerical solvers, partial differential algebraic equations and flowsheet monitoring, with the COBIA binary interoperability architecture as the next step. Use is global; members include software vendors and operating companies, and CO-LaN awards yearly prizes. Specifications and experience reports are published on the CO-LaN site; no licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: support differs between simulators and specification versions. For simulation it lets models from different vendors be coupled in one process flowsheet, useful for plant digital twins and safety studies. Related catalogue records include DWSIM and Aspen HYSYS.
